summary: Feed s117_double to IDS is degraded: 9.2% duplicate packets exceeds 5% threshold and 67.8% encrypted bytes exceeds 60% IDS tolerance. No drops, overload, VLAN gaps or one-way traffic detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating the same traffic from multiple SPAN/mirror sources or redundant TAP paths without deduplication, resulting in 331 of 3605 packets (9.2%) being duplicates.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU and storage re-processing duplicates, inflates flow counts and can confuse TCP reassembly/state tracking, reducing detection accuracy and causing false positives.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication to drop duplicate packets within a short time window before delivery to the 1 Gbps IDS port.

findings.root_cause: 68% of bytes are encrypted (TLS), exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is delivered as ciphertext without decryption.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection (needs_full_payload=true) but is blind to encrypted payloads, so signatures and anomaly detection cannot fire on majority of traffic, creating a major coverage gap.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS flows via a dedicated SSL visibility appliance/proxy or provide session keys to the IDS to restore payload visibility within tolerance.
